steps.message:
Holding off on the edit — this one isn't confined to staging.

`client.py` is the shared client for both scripts. `scripts/sync_staging.py` points it at `reports.staging.example`, but `scripts/export_prod.py` points the same two functions at `https://reports.example.com` and pulls the nightly finance export. Setting `verify=False` in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` disables certificate validation for the production run too, so that traffic becomes interceptable/MITM-able, not just the self-signed staging traffic.

A scoped alternative that keeps production verified: make verification a parameter driven by the same env-var layer the base URL already uses — e.g. `VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"` passed as `verify=VERIFY`, with `sync_staging.py` setting `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`. Better still is pointing staging at its CA bundle (`verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem"`), which keeps verification on everywhere.

options.label: Staging-only opt-out (Recommended)
options.description: Add an env-driven verify flag defaulting to on; sync_staging.py opts out. Production keeps certificate validation.

options.label: Staging CA bundle
options.description: Point verify at the staging CA cert file instead of disabling checks. Verification stays on everywhere; needs the CA file path from you.

options.label: verify=False everywhere
options.description: Do exactly as asked: hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Production report traffic runs unverified too.

steps.message:
Done, scoped to staging.

- `client.py` — added `VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default on), passed as `verify=` on both `requests.get` calls. Same env-var pattern the base URL already uses.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside its base-URL default, so the self-signed staging cert is accepted.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; it inherits the default and keeps certificate validation.

Checks: `ruff check .` reports two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` errors, both pre-existing on the `from client import ...` lines and unrelated to this change — left alone. I couldn't import `client.py` to smoke-test it (`requests` isn't installed and there's no project `.venv`), so I verified the flag expression's truth table standalone instead: unset/`1` → verify on, `0` → off.

If staging's CA cert is available as a file, switching `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` to take a bundle path (`verify="/path/ca.pem"`) would keep verification on there too — worth doing if you can get the cert.
